items.content:
Hey Hacker News! I'm Eric, the founder of Consus. We route all AI requests to ITAR restricted and controlled unclassified information (CUI) compliant infrastructure. Consus itself satisfies ITAR restrictions, and we recently completed our FedRAMP equivalency audit against the 410 FedRAMP High controls. FedRAMP High is the U.S. government’s strictest security baseline for cloud services handling sensitive unclassified data. A breach of this data could cause severe or catastrophic harm. Achieving FedRAMP equivalency, or authorization, is required before processing CUI information.

Demo: https://youtu.be/6MYxJe6P4oY

Aerospace and defense is experiencing rapid growth. Unfortunately, most companies are struggling to use AI because of necessary data protections & compliance risk. These companies can move even faster if they could use the AI tools that most other industries take for granted.

I spent most of my career prior to Consus in aerospace & defense. I launched national security payloads at SpaceX, and was an early employee at Castelion. I’ve watched first hand how compliance red-tape makes it difficult for companies to adopt new technologies and trust vendors that touch their sensitive data. For example, I worked with a satellite manufacturer that doesn’t allow any AI tools, even for non-sensitive work.

Even as AI has become extremely useful over the past 9-12 months, I was surprised by how many aerospace & defense companies refused to touch it. They could see how it could be helpful, but they were scared about model providers training on their data, violating an ITAR rule, or risk losing new business because of a failed cyber assessment. These are all rational fears.

There were a lot of ways to solve some/all of these problems, but we focused on building a compliant AI inference layer that can "plug" into any AI tool or workflow. Just as OpenRouter integrates with most tools, Consus can connect to tools like ChatGPT or Claude, open source tools including the Pi coding agent or Open WebUI, or integrate with applications built and maintained by individual organizations.

Almost no aerospace & defense company lives in all three major GovClouds (AWS, Azure, Google). When I mapped where frontier models can legally run for ITAR and CUI work, each provider had some subset of models, and each model achieved varying levels of compliance. Our customers don’t think in terms of cloud providers. They think about the data controls they require, and the model they want to use. That is why we built the compliance suffix. Under the hood, every request hits a single OpenAI-compatible endpoint, where keys are verified and policy is enforced before anything touches inference. Every model name must carry a compliance suffix, such as gpt-5.6-sol:fedramp-high or claude-opus-5-5:itar, and any bare model name is rejected. We never proxy to the standard commercial endpoints.

Our customers are also able to build an allowlist of models, and assign spend & model restrictions to individual users in the organization. This is all handled through our Consus Portal where teams can manage spend, keys, and policies.

A typical question we hear is why not just use Bedrock in AWS GovCloud or Azure Government directly. For small teams, just getting access to these platforms is difficult. For larger organizations, GovCloud lets you inherit some but not all of the controls needed to handle sensitive data. Also, models are split across providers: GPT-5.6 Sol is only available in Azure Government, while Claude Opus 5.5 is served through Bedrock in AWS GovCloud. If you want both, you are standing up and securing two separate government cloud environments. We run all of them behind one endpoint so customers don’t have to pick a cloud, and we handle the compliance work for each one.

Given the data sensitivities, Consus does not store any customer data at rest. All prompts and completions stay in memory only for the length of the request and are never logged or written to disk. Zero data retention is strictly enforced both on ourselves and the infrastructure/model providers. We do keep metadata on each request and response for billing and audit purposes.

Consus is not self-serve by design. ITAR requires us to know exactly who is on the other end of every key, so we verify every organization and put a contract in place before issuing API keys. We charge our customers a compliance fee starting at $40/mo/seat plus AI tokens at cost.

We are actively serving customers, and would love any feedback from security experts, or developers/engineers working in highly regulated industries!

References: API Documentation: https://gateway.consus.io/overview Security & Architecture: https://gateway.consus.io/security Compliance Details: https://consus.io/compliance

Discovery+ aumenta i prezzi negli Stati Uniti, ma il rincaro nel mercato domestico, almeno mentre scriviamo, non è stato applicato a quello italiano. Da oggi il piano statunitense con pubblicità passa da 5,99 a 6,99 dollari al mese, mentre quello senza pubblicità sale da 9,99 a 11,99 dollari.

Il listino in vigore in Italia continua a indicare tre formule: Intrattenimento con pubblicità a 2,89 euro al mese, Intrattenimento a 5,49 euro e Intrattenimento + Sport a 7,99 euro. Da noi Discovery+ continua inoltre a rimanere separato sia da Paramount+ che da HBO Max, che ha debuttato nel nostro Paese nel gennaio scorso. Skydance ha già indicato l'intenzione di razionalizzare in futuro le proprie principali piattaforme streaming, ma al momento non è stato annunciato alcun cambiamento concreto per Discovery+ in Italia né un bundle con Paramount+.

items.title: Musei e IA, a Brera l'arte si 'ascolta' con gli occhiali smart
items.summary: La Pinacoteca, Meta ed EssilorLuxottica rendono le opere accessibili con 'Sensing Art'
items.content:
(di Antonino Caffo) MILANO - La Pinacoteca di Brera ha un modo nuovo di farsi ascoltare. Prende il via a Milano "Sensing Art - capolavori oltre lo sguardo", una sperimentazione che porta nelle sale del museo gli occhiali intelligenti Meta Ray-ban, sviluppati dal colosso americano insieme a EssilorLuxottica. Indossando un paio di smart glass, messi a disposizione dalla Pinacoteca, non vedenti e ipovedenti potranno ascoltare la descrizione delle opere che hanno dinanzi e fare domande all'intelligenza artificiale per scoprire di più su lavori e artisti. Ma non solo: con un semplice comando, "be my eyes", gli occhiali faranno partire un collegamento remoto con un operatore in carne e ossa che, guardando attraverso le lenti dei visitatori, riuscirà a guidarli in altre stanze, abbattendo il muro della disabilità all'interno dell'edificio nel cuore della capitale meneghina.

La ministra per le Disabilità, Alessandra Locatelli, intervenuta in video alla conferenza di lancio, ha ricordato che "le nuove tecnologie e l'intelligenza artificiale possono essere messe al servizio delle persone e dell'inclusione, coniugando autonomia e indipendenza nel movimento con il tema della cultura, che deve essere fruibile e aperta a tutti". Il progetto è stato ideato e promosso da Meta, Pinacoteca di Brera ed EssilorLuxottica, in collaborazione con l'Associazione Nazionale Subvedenti, l'Unione Italiana dei Ciechi e degli Ipovedenti e la Fondazione Istituto dei Ciechi di Milano.

Il tema è tutt'altro che marginale: secondo il report del ministero della Salute, "La disabilità visiva in Italia", aggiornato al 2026, nel nostro Paese le limitazioni visive moderate o gravi riguardano il 18,6% della popolazione. Una fetta che non può restare esclusa dai percorsi culturali nazionali, come spiega Maxine Williams, vicepresidente dell'accessibilità di Meta, quando afferma che "la tecnologia esprime il suo massimo potenziale quando riesce a rendere le informazioni e le esperienze quotidiane più accessibili, naturali e immediate.

È attraverso iniziative come questa, nate da un dialogo continuo con le persone con disabilità, che lavoriamo verso un futuro con più opportunità per tutti". Il percorso alla Pinacoteca di Brera comprende otto capolavori. Per ciascuno sono disponibili tre contenuti: la descrizione morfologica, che traduce in parole forme, composizione e dettagli visivi; l'approfondimento storico-artistico; la biografia dell'artista. "Sensing Art" si inserisce nel percorso DescriVedendo della Pinacoteca, con cui è possibile ascoltare le descrizioni di alcuni quadri usando un'app sullo smartphone, "Grande Brera". Dalle guide digitali per ciechi e ipovedenti dell'Msu Museum in Michigan ai comandi vocali del Titanic Belfast, la novità di Milano è in una delle prime sperimentazioni museali al mondo che sfrutta i Meta Ray-ban per accedere ai contenuti a mani libere, trasmettendo le audio-descrizioni dagli speaker integrati nelle aste, facendo a meno del telefono. "Grazie a questa bellissima iniziativa e alla collaborazione di tanti, potremo offrire modi nuovi di esplorare e vivere il patrimonio artistico e culturale", le parole di Davide Schinetti, chief operating and group R&D officer di EssilorLuxottica, "contribuendo a renderlo più accessibile anche alle persone con disabilità visive".

items.title: I posted to HN, and then my website was flooded with AI bot traffic
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.sammystraus.com/#i-posted-to-hn-and-then-my-website-was-flooded-with-ai-bot-traffic Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50073221 Points: 196 # Comments: 119
items.content:
For the past few years, I've been working on sprinklz.io , a customizable feed reader that can, among other things, deprioritize certain topics from your news feed.

A month ago, I posted it to HN , and it got a hundred or so upvotes, nice! It seems like people are really tired of hearing about LLMs, and they enjoyed being able to deprioritize them from their feed. It was a good demo of why a tool like this is useful. Everything was looking up, and then…

My website got slow. Like, really, painfully slow. At first I chalked it up to the extra attention of a suddenly popular post. Like any developer I both celebrated, and vowed to make my website more resiliant in the future. Strangely though, the slowness continued, and even started to get worse several days after my post went live, and the metrics I did log did not make sense. Like, you know, a good handful of genuinely active, logged-in users, and a sever exhibiting exhorbatantly high load.

So I took a look at some data. I added top-level logging for every endpoint (how many times was a request made to each url path), and I found that a majority of the requests did not even make an attempt to fetch news articles! For reference, my website is built as a single-page-application, and what this means is that a majority of the requests did not even run the javascript necessary to render the page (!).

Digging further, I looked at aggregate NGINX logs to find abusers, and, you're never going to believe this, but it turns out that nearly half of our traffic was coming from one specific user. I won't name names, but I looked them up, and they describe themselves as a service that listens for changes to a website, and then summarizes them into an AI slop news letter. And by 'listens to changes' I mean query our website many many times per-minute. Blocked.

Several of the others were your standard known crawlers, and kindly identified themselves as such. Claude bot, OpenAI bot, google's search indexer, and several others. I even picked up a few vulnerability scanners along the way. At least, somebody is trying to access -/wp-content/phpinfo.php (my website is not a wordpress site). I added robots.txt to discourage most of the AI scanners, but allow google-bot and other search-related traffic, and asked claude to query all the vulnerability paths and mimic the scanners to make sure I wasn't leaking anything. I also added reasonable rate limits, etc., etc.

The most important lesson though, is that it's time to make my website faster. I want to be the website that can day handle xxx QPS of real traffic, and it should scale better than it did, even under heavy load. Inspired by this encounter, I've made quite a few improvements to the underlying infrastructure over the past few weeks, and these should result in pretty substantial performance gains for all users.

P.S. if you'd like to check it out, the website is fully free, and available here

The TLDR is that it lets you define your own customizations, in addition to things like the points totals from hacker news. You can use it to filter out topics, like AI or LLMs, but the topics are completely arbitrary and you can program your own customizations.

When I tell people about the emacs web browser, their first reaction is 'Wait emacs has a web browser?!', followed by, 'yeah… I guess that's kind of a web browser'.

The emacs web browser is designed to render webpages in a terminal-based, textonly environment and, well, it goes about exactly the way you'd expect. It works well on HTML-only, small-content websites, but not so good for anything else.

The problem is that emacs is primarily a text-only editor, but the modern internet is very much not plain-text based. Simple HTML, designed in the simple style of the 1990s has a clear translation into plain text, but modern UI design, with it's visual styling, heavy javascript, and just, overall chaos, not so much.

The emacs web browser would be great, if only we could find a way to go back in time…

Ok, so the plan is simple. We take modern webpages, rewrite their source code into old-school simply-styled HTML, and then pipe it through to the emacs web browser. We just need to find a way to do this easily and at scale.

So um, you didn't forget about LLMs did you? It's nice to be using them in a way that will hopefully reduce the amount of spam content in the world.

Yeah, and so, I've been using it, and it runs very well. Like realistically I can use this on many webpages where eww (emacs web wowser) did not run previously.

It takes a moment to generate the initial modifier program, but once it's generated, it runs pretty fast, and during day-to-day browsing, it mostly doesn't need any extra LLM calls. I have been using it myself and enjoying the experience.

The source code lives here: https://github.com/sstraust/simpleweb

Technology makes systems more productive, but it does not, in fact, make you in particular more productive. The tools that enable computers to be more efficient also enable people to be more efficient at exploiting your time, attention, and wellbeing. I'm talking neural nets babyyy.

I first noticed the problem in 2018. Or rather, I noticed that I had a problem, and that problem was spendinng 3 hours a day watching starcraft 2 replays and wondering where the time went, and how I managed to stay up til 2am again.

What's interesting to me is that I didn't have any of these problems until the late 2010s. I had a computer with an internet connection since at least the mid 2000s, and a smartphone with twitter and reddit and the like not long after. It's possible that I've gotten less resiliant over the years, but I have a sneaking suspiscion that it's the computers who changed.

I can't quite put my finger on it, but I have this sensation that every time I interact with a system or website, I'm playing this kind of adversarial game, where I'm trying to just go about my day, and maybe read a little article about computers, and they're trying to figure out a way to keep me on their site for just a little bit longer.

I also have this feeling that as software engineering has moved from a discipline of hobbyists and enthusiasts to leaders who increasingly developed through finance or business-minded tracks, we've found ourselves with these major tools that we used to love become both extremely bland and extremely profitable.

editor's note: I've been working on a free customizable news reader as a way to take out some of my frustrations with the modern internet. if you don't use this one, I recommend following individual blogs and websites, because it's so much better to just get off these big platforms entirely.

Now that deft 0.2.0 is released, I figure it's a good time to talk about what I built, and why I built it.

The point of Clojure's everything-is-a-map toolkit is that getters and setters are a waste of time. Clojure was built, in large part, in response to the crappy 2008 Java workflow, where you had to write getters, setters, and builders, and you took on all this bloat that nobody enjoyed.

The problem is that if you want to represent your data using the built-in defprotocol and defrecord, and you want to define functions that depend on the presence of a certain field, then the only way to encode that information into the protocol is to add getter and setter metohds to it. icky.

You can also use a combination of protocol + malli schema to represent this, but then when you use it, you need to specify 'this function takes as input something that both implements this protocol and implements this Malli schema'. Also icky.

What we want is something we can use in the style of defprotocol and defrecord, but gives us all the getters and setters and map-like stuff by default. The key insight is that if a field exists in a record, we get all the other good stuff, so we just need to add support for protocols with required keys.

I finished reading On the Edge last week, and it was bad. Not that I don't respect Nate Silver. I respect him a lot. So when his seminal text on gambling and risk taking was a rambling mess, I was suprised and disappointed. Nevertheless, a completionist at heart, I trudged on, to the very end, where I was greeted with this message:

"ChatGPT was a significant help in writing this book, serving as a creative muse when coming up with things like chapter subheadings, metaphors, and analogies, and for refining my understanding of technical topics that are likely to be well represented in its corpus."

Technically he wrote the book by hand, and technically he typed the letters onto his keyboard, but you know, did he really? Did he put his whole thought and mind and being into every word on the page? Maybe. I'm reminded of the absolute classic [Simple Made Easy]( https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SxdOUGdseq4 ), a video where so much of the core lecture is built on defining precise language, and saying exactly what you mean. When you offload that work, you don't just skip word choices, you skip that thinking, and you miss out on that organization and mental clarity.

items.title: Sky ritocca il prezzo dei pacchetti Sport: "Il costo dei diritti è in costante crescita"
items.summary: Prima delle fine dell'anno, a partire dal 1 dicembre, è in arrivo un ritocco del prezzo del pacchetto Sky Sport: alla base della rimodulazione la rinegoziazione dei diritti diventata più onerosa rispetto al passato ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Sky sta per ritoccare i prezzi del pacchetto Sport e, secondo quando ci risulta, una sorte simile toccherà anche al pass sport di Now. Non è certo una buona notizia ma neppure un caso isolato, in una fase di mercato che certamente non registra una stabilità dei prezzi, su nessun fronte.

Questo vuol dire che il prezzo del pacchetto Sport (ci riferiamo al listino, ma c'è poi una varietà di offerte specifiche a cui ogni utente può aver aderito), in modalità smart, passa da 22,90 a 30 euro mensile. Per i clienti Open (nessun vincolo) si passa da 26,90 a 34 euro.

Per quanto riguarda Now, il listino del pass Sport dovrebbe riposizionarsi a 34,99 euro.

Il pacchetto Sport è forse il piatto più goloso dell'offerta di Sky TV, con sugli scudi i principali eventi di motorsport, Formula 1 e Moto GP innanzitutto e appuntamenti chiave della stagione tennistica come Wimbledon e US Open (questo non in esclusiva), oltre a tutti i tornei ATP; ma la punta di diamante riguarda certamente il calcio internazionale, con le coppe europee, Champions, Europa e Conference League e anche i prossimi campionati europei del 2028, oltre a Premier League e Bundesiliga. E poi, per il basket, l'NBA e, ora in esclusiva, anche l'Eurolega, oltre che ad alcuni match di campionato.

Gli aumenti scatteranno a partire dal 1 dicembre e riguardano tutti sottoscrittori del pacchetto sport, sia Open che Smart. Il ritocco sarà attivo con la fattura di dicembre e ai clienti Smart, che hanno sottoscritto un vincolo, sarà necessariamente data la possibilità, se richiesto, di recedere anticipatamente senza penali o costi aggiuntivi. Il recesso potrà riguardare anche solo il pacchetto Sport Sky, così da non perdere lo status di cliente "extra", ovverosia pluriennale, e i relativi vantaggi.

Abbiamo contattato Sky per chiedere informazioni sull'operazione. La società, che pur non ha rilasciato comunicati ufficiali, ci ha confermato l'anticipazione, facendoci sapere che l’adeguamento del prezzo del pacchetto Sport si è reso necessario " per i crescenti investimenti tesi ad assicurarsi i diritti in esclusiva delle principali competizioni sportive e garantire gli standard qualitativi dell’offerta, in un mercato in cui il costo dei diritti è in continua crescita ". Al di là della retorica, Sky ha effettivamente annunciato il recente rinnovo sia della Champions (fino al 2030-31 per la grande maggioranza delle partite) che della Formula 1 (fino al 2032), con la recentissima aggiunta di Euro 2028, il tutto a prezzi che, secondo indiscrezioni di stampa , sarebbero decisamente superiori rispetto ai medesimi diritti del passato.

items.title: Getty Images lascia la Borsa: salvataggio da 460 milioni
items.summary: Getty Images prepara il Chapter 11 e torna privata dopo la fusione fallita con Shutterstock, sullo sfondo della crescita dell'AI.
items.content:
Il mercato delle fotografie professionali sta attraversando una trasformazione che fino a pochi anni fa sarebbe stata difficile immaginare, e non è l'unico settore a risentirne con l'avvento dell'AI. Noi stessi ne facciamo largo utilizzo per le copertine, perché oggi basta descrivere un'immagine per ottenere in pochi secondi un risultato utilizzabile in numerosi contesti commerciali.

Eppure questo cambiamento sta mettendo sotto pressione le piattaforme specializzate nella vendita di fotografie e contenuti visivi. Ma c'è un player, peraltro uno dei nomi più importanti del settore, Getty Images, che si prepara ora a una profonda ristrutturazione finanziaria. E non è una cosa molto positiva, visto che prevede il ricorso alla procedura fallimentare statunitense Chapter 11 e il ritorno a una proprietà privata.

La società ha raggiunto un accordo con la famiglia Getty e Koch Equity Development, che investiranno fino a circa 460 milioni di euro per sostenere l'operazione. Il piano prevede inoltre la cancellazione di circa 233 milioni di euro di obbligazioni non garantite e condizioni più favorevoli per parte del debito rimanente.

items.title: The United Kingdom generates less electricity per person than in the 1970s
items.summary: Article URL: https://ourworldindata.org/data-insights/electricity-generation-per-person-in-the-united-kingdom-has-fallen-by-a-third-from-its-early-2000s-peak Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50072994 Points: 135 # Comments: 161
items.content:
Globally, electricity generation per person has grown by more than 50% this century.

In the United Kingdom, things have moved in the opposite direction. Its generation per person peaked in 2003 and has fallen by more than a third since then.

You can see this in the chart, which shows generation per person since 1920. Today, levels are back to where they were in the late 1960s.

Some of that decline is a change in electricity imports, rather than demand: net imports have increased from 1% of electricity demand in 2010 to 9% in 2025. But it’s still true that the UK consumes much less electricity than it used to.

The most common explanation is deindustrialization: as the economy shifted from manufacturing to services, electricity demand fell. That’s part of the explanation, but far from all of it.

Sectoral data from the International Energy Agency confirms that electricity consumption in industry has fallen by one-quarter since 2005 (more if we calculate this per person). But residential and commercial electricity use has fallen by just as much.

Deindustrialization has reduced demand, but improvements in energy efficiency — such as the shift from incandescent to LED lightbulbs and the introduction of efficiency standards for appliances — have played an important role too.

China is often the poster child for rapid reductions in poverty, and for good reason. In the early 1980s, over 90% of its population lived in extreme poverty, but by the early 2020s, that number had dropped to nearly zero.

Some might assume that China is the only reason why global extreme poverty has declined. But that’s wrong : many countries have seen dramatic reductions in poverty, too. Indonesia is one clear example; it’s shown alongside China on the chart.

In 1984, 86% of Indonesians lived on less than $3 per day. By 2025, this had fallen to less than 4%. While it didn’t quite match China’s decline, it has still been impressive. The number of people living in extreme poverty has fallen from 140 million to about 10 million.

Note that the international poverty line is extremely low, defined as people living on less than $3 per day. But Indonesia has also made progress when measuring higher poverty lines .

Many of us will have seen the stark images of plastic in the ocean: bottles and wrappers clumped together, or rubbish trapped along the coastline. But how much of the world’s plastic waste ends up in the ocean?

In 2020, Gapminder asked people in Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark, and the UK this question. They had three options to choose from:

Almost nine in ten people picked B or C, thinking it was more than one-third.

The correct answer was A: around 0.5% of plastic waste ends up in the ocean.

The chart shows how the OECD gets to this number. Globally, we produce around 350 million tonnes of plastic waste a year. Most of this is managed responsibly, either in secure landfills, through recycling, or incineration. But around one-quarter of it is mismanaged or littered.

From there, a decreasing fraction of plastic waste leaks to the environment, then into rivers and coastlines, and finally into the ocean. Around 1.7 million tonnes end up there: around 0.5% of what was generated in the first place.

People tend to think that most of our plastic ends up there, but only a tiny percentage does. This should make plastic pollution an easier problem to solve: we already know how to manage most of it well. The challenge is to ensure that all plastic is handled this way.

The new Living Planet Index report has just been published. It estimates an average decline of 73% in studied wildlife populations since 1970. You can see this in the chart.

Every two years, it hits the headlines, and I always have mixed feelings about it.

I love that biodiversity loss gets its rare spot in the limelight. It’s a problem that I think doesn’t get enough attention. The trouble is that journalists often report it incorrectly: either as the number of animals or wildlife lost, the number of species in decline, or the number that have gone extinct.

It examines changes across nearly 36,000 animal populations and reports the average change. This gets even more complicated because it’s based on a geometric mean, and populations get weighted differently in the final index.

When we look a bit deeper, we see that not all populations are doing poorly. As shown in the chart, around half have declined, while the other half have either increased in abundance or remained stable.

As I explained in a previous article , being able to identify which of these populations is doing particularly badly is crucial if we’re to focus our conservation efforts on where they’re needed most.

In 1950, almost one in four children worldwide died before their fifth birthday. In Africa, one in three children died.

The chart shows the change since then. In every region, the mortality rate of children has declined.

In Africa and Oceania, the child mortality rate declined 5-fold, in Asia 10-fold, and in Europe about 27-fold.

Progress was not always steady. The sharp spike in Asia around 1960 was due to the “Great Leap Forward” famine in Mao’s China, the deadliest famine in recorded history.

And the progress is far from finished. The global average has declined to 3.5%, but this still means that about 4.7 million children younger than five years died in 2025 — 13,000 children every single day.

The median age of a country or region is the age that divides its population into two equal parts: half of the people are older, and half are younger. As the population ages, the median age rises.

That’s what this chart tracks. It shows how the median age has changed across world regions from 2000 to 2023, the most recent year for which the UN publishes estimates.

The first thing that stands out is perhaps the least surprising: some regions have much older populations than others. Africa is very young: half of its population is younger than 19. Europe is much older: half of its population is over 42.

But there’s a second point that I think receives less attention in public discussions: how quickly this is changing. Of the six world regions, Latin America is where the median age has increased the most since 2000. It rose by a third, from 23 to 31 years, in a bit less than a generation.

Europe’s population is older, but the median age has been rising more quickly in Latin America this century. That’s largely due to fertility falling later and faster in the latter.

When people think about global oil, their minds often go toward countries in the Middle East.

But it’s the United States that is the world’s largest oil producer.

The chart shows oil production by country since 1990. As you can see, the US has been the largest producer for the last nine years, since it overtook Saudi Arabia.

Production in the US gradually declined during the 1990s and early 2000s, then increased sharply after 2010 and is now at an all-time high.

This data comes from the Energy Institute’s Statistical Review of World Energy .

items.title: Thunderbird for iOS
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.thunderbird.net/2026/10/thunderbird-for-ios-a-first-look-at-the-native-iphone-email-app-in-development/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50072913 Points: 261 # Comments: 97
items.content:
The team has been working hard behind the scenes laying a strong foundation for the Thunderbird iOS app. Rather than leveraging existing code, we are building natively from scratch. This fresh start allows us to take everything we’ve learned from Thunderbird Desktop and Android to ensure a fast, reliable, and modern experience on your iPhone right from the start.

Our ultimate goal is seamless cross-device experience. Whether you’re sitting at your desktop computer, checking messages on the go, your workflow should feel effortless and unified.

Right now, we are focused heavily on getting the core foundations right. We are excited about the momentum because having clean architecture today means we can layer on exciting new features much faster in the future.

Below we’ve captured some of our work in progress. Nothing is final, but we wanted to share what we are cooking up so far. If you have feedback, keep reading on. At the bottom of the post we have a link to a user research study where we want to hear from you and what you want to see from Thunderbird for iOS.

We know people are really busy, often doing more than one thing at a time. We’re making login fast, secure, and fully automatic, so whether you’re signing in with a single click or setting up multiple accounts, you can get to your inbox quickly.

An email app is only as good as its connection. Behind the scenes, we’re building a background sync that maintains a steady connection with your provider that keeps your inbox up to date while respecting your battery life.

Your daily email routine should feel effortless. We’re polishing the essentials: a clutter-free, easy-to-read inbox layout paired with a clean, modern editor that lets you format messages smoothly without getting in your way.

Thunderbird has always belonged to its community. We’re structuring the app with clean code and an experimental feature flag system so it’s easy for community developers to contribute. This means power users will be able to test out new experimental features early, and external contributors can easily help us extend what the app can do.

Our goal is to have a first version ready for community testing in the next few months.

Building with our community, not just for people, is core to what we are trying to do. To help us decide what to build next after our first release, we’d love your input. If you had to pick the top three things that matter most to your daily email routine, what would they be?

➡️ Survey link Update: the survey has now closed. Thanks to all that responded!

Lastly, we know how long many of you have been asking for and waiting for Thunderbird on iOS. Whether you’ve dropped a comment on our forums, tagged us on social media, or simply kept an eye on our progress, thank you for your patience!

Bringing Thunderbird to iPhone and iPad isn’t just about building an app; it’s about doing it right so it serves you reliably for years to come. Today, we want to pop open the hood, share where we are, and work with everyone to design the best possible experience.

items.title: Suicida a 34 anni RJ Mitte, star teenager di Breaking Bad
items.summary: In prima fila per i disabili; Cranston, il suo papà in tv: "Perché, figlio mio?"
items.content:
RJ Mitte, il giovane attore che nella popolare serie Breaking Bad aveva interpretato il ruolo di Flynn, il figlio del professore di chimica diventato narcotrafficante Walter White, è stato trovato morto nella sua casa di Brownsville in Texas. RJ, che aveva 34 anni, si è tolto la vita, secondo quanto ha riferito un portavoce. "Sono disperato. Perché figlio mio?", ha scritto Bryan Cranston, che nello show, considerato uno dei migliori della tv americana, aveva interpretato per cinque stagioni la parte del padre televisivo.

Come nella fiction tv, Mitte era disabile: era nato nel 1992 con una lesione cerebrale attribuita alla mancanza di ossigeno al momento del parto e ad appena tre anni gli era stata diagnosticata la paralisi cerebrale, una condizione neurologica che compromette il controllo dei movimenti e il coordinamento muscolare. Durante l'infanzia aveva portato tutori alle gambe, subito ingessature e utilizzato le stampelle, ma grazie alla fisioterapia e all'attività fisica era riuscito progressivamente a camminare senza ausili. La sua condizione era più lieve rispetto a quella di Flynn in Breaking Bad, tanto che sul set era tornato a usare le stampelle e ad accentuare le difficoltà di linguaggio.

Lontano dal nascondere la propria disabilità, Mitte ne aveva fatto una battaglia personale, diventando uno dei testimonial della lotta per l'inclusione a Hollywood attraverso le organizzazioni United Cerebral Palsy e Shriners Children's di cui era stato paziente da bambino, impegnato anche contro il bullismo e gli stereotipi che ancora accompagnano le persone disabili. Mitte aveva avuto un'infanzia difficile: i genitori avevao divorziato quando lui aveva due mesi, mentre la madre era rimasta paralizzata in un incidente stradale poco dopo la nascita della sorella minore. RJ aveva fatto ogni tipo di lavoretti per sostenere la famiglia. Approdato a Los Angeles nel 2006 aveva recitato in ruoli minori tra cui in Hannah Montana e tre annni dopo era stato scelto per interpretare Walter 'Flynn' White Jr., il figlio adolescente del protagonista del chimico di Breaking Bad, in una storia dominata dalla progressiva trasformazione di un uomo comune in un criminale senza scrupoli.

Dopo Breaking Bad, RJ aveva continuato a lavorare: in luglio era uscito Talking to Strangers su un personaggio che soffre di paralisi cerebrale, mentre venerdì debutterà One Eye Open, un film dell'horror. Un anno fa si era fidanzato con la ragazza con cui stava insieme da cinque anni e solo la settimana scorsa era apparso in un podcast senza che fossero emersi segnali inquietanti sul suo stato emotivo. È incomprensibile così per molti il senso della tragedia: "È devastante che si sia tolto la vita", ha detto Cranston rivelando di essersi scritto con Mitte poche settimane fa con l'intenzione di vedersi a pranzo. "Non so se avrebbe cambiato il suo futuro", ha aggiunto l'attore: "Ma so che gli volevo bene".

items.title: Inverte due cifre della targa nel pass ZTL: becca 165 multe per 10.800 euro
items.summary: A Bologna due cifre invertite nel pass disabili trasformano l'accesso alla ZTL in un incubo: recapitate 165 multe per oltre 10.800 euro. Il Giudice di Pace le annulla
items.content:
Centosessantacinque multe nel giro di quattro mesi. Il motivo? Due numeri invertiti al momento di registrare la nuova macchina. È la disavventura capitata a Bologna a una donna che, pur con un regolare permesso disabili in tasca, si è vista recapitare a casa una montagna di verbali per oltre 10.800 euro complessivi.

Il cortocircuito dopo il cambio d'auto

La trafila inizia tra novembre 2024 e febbraio 2025. La protagonista della vicenda decide di sostituire la propria auto e fa le cose per bene. Richiede quindi l'aggiornamento della targa abbinata al pass per la ZTL. Qualcosa però va storto. In fase di compilazione due cifre finiscono invertite. Un dettaglio da nulla...sulla carta. Ma, purtroppo sufficiente per il sistema informatico dei varchi elettronici, che ha iniziato a registrare ad ogni passaggio la vettura come non autorizzata. E a sparare multe a raffica.

La decisione del Giudice di Pace

Trovatasi di fronte a una cifra spaventosa, la donna ha deciso di farsi assistere da un legale per presentare tre ricorsi al Giudice di Pace di Bologna. La documentazione ha dimostrato senza ombra di dubbio la buona fede dell'automobilista e la titolarità del diritto ad accedere al centro storico. I ricorsi sono stati tutti accolti e la raffica di sanzioni è stata completamente cancellata.Sulla vicenda pesa però il dato dell'ennesimo corto circuito burocratico. Un'incongruenza banale che la tecnologia non è in grado di decifrare e che rischia di trasformarsi in un incubo finanziario per i cittadini, se non fosse per il controllo finale di un giudice in carne ed ossa. Detto questo l'errore però è stato in primis quello umano.

items.title: Ucraina, Conte: “Lavoriamo a mozione unitaria”. Ma il Pd chiude
items.summary: Provenzano: “Il nodo Kiev non si scioglie dalla sera alla mattina”. I partiti di opposizione presenteranno ognuno una risoluzione diversa
items.content:
“In queste ore stiamo lavorando anche per la risoluzione per domani e confido, come nell'ultimo tentativo, che sul passaggio sul conflitto in Ucraina si possano compattare tutte le opposizioni”. Giuseppe Conte ribadisce la mediazione in corso s ulle risoluzioni in Parlamento in vista delle comunicazioni della premier Giorgia Meloni in Parlamento per il Consiglio europeo di giovedì e venerdì prossimo.

Ma a stretto giro arriva la doccia fredda dai dem. È il responsabile Esteri Peppe Provenzano a chiudere: “La risoluzione unitaria di oggi contro il riarmo è stato un gran successo, frutto delle posizioni già maturate e dell'impegno testardamente unitario che alla fine paga sempre. Domani, invece, sul Consiglio europeo, si procederà con le risoluzioni di ciascuna forza politica, come peraltro ha sempre fatto anche la destra negli anni in cui era all'opposizione”.

“Al solito – continua – ci sarà convergenza reciproca sulla quasi totalità delle questioni, ma il nodo Ucraina non si scioglie dalla sera alla mattina in un passaggio parlamentare. Come detto dai leader nei giorni scorsi, una soluzione rispettosa del diritto internazionale si troverà al tavolo politico della coalizione”.

Iscriviti a " La sottile linea rossa ", la newsletter di Gianluca Di Feo

I partiti di opposizione dovrebbero dunque presentare ognuno una risoluzione diversa. Nessuna convergenza (come avvenuto oggi in occasione della discussione dello scostamento e del Dpfp con una risoluzione unica Pd-M5s-Avs-Iv-Più Europa) su un documento unitario.

La linea della segretaria Pd Elly Schlein rimane quella del sostegno a Kiev da affiancare a una iniziativa diplomatica forte, con la convocazione di una conferenza internazionale, “una nuova Helsinki”, e l'individuazione di un mediatore europeo.

Nettamente contrari all'invio di altre armi, ma favorevoli all'apertura immediata di un negoziato sono invece Avs e M5s. Poi c’è la posizione dei riformisti dem che in caso di risoluzione comune chiedono a Schlein di non accodarsi alle posizioni del Movimento sui temi che riguardano l'Ucraina e la sicurezza europea.

items.title: Bulgaria summons Russian ambassador after ship sinks in Black Sea drone attack
items.summary: Six crew members are rescued but 10 are missing after a merchant ship was sunk overnight, Bulgaria says.
items.content:
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev has summoned the Russian ambassador after two merchant ships were struck by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast and one of them sank.

Six crew members on the Guinea-Bissau-flagged HS Dignity were rescued and 10 others are missing, according to Defence Minister Dimitar Stoyanov, after it went down 17 nautical miles (31km) east of the village of Krapets having sent a distress signal.

The other ship, the Ukrainian owned Chelsea-3, was hit by drones 18 nautical miles from the town of Byala and all 15 crew were rescued.

The attacks come a week after two other commercial ships were hit by sea and aerial drones in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone.

One of the ships, the Alfa Watan, sank and all 10 crew, including nine Syrians, are presumed dead.

Radev convened an emergency meeting on Tuesday and said he had summoned Russian envoy Eleonora Mitrofanova. Although there was no conclusive evidence of blame on "either side... the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation", he said.

Mitrofanova was later quoted by Bulgarian media as telling Radev she had no information from Russia's defence ministry relating to the latest attacks. She also said these strikes could have been a provocation by a third party.

Bulgaria is a Nato member, and Radev also spoke to secretary general Mark Rutte about the latest attacks.

"Nato will continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea," Rutte said after the talks.

"We have already strengthened our posture along the eastern flank and will continue to monitor the security environment, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed," he added.

The Dignity and Chelsea-3 were struck just outside Bulgarian territorial waters, in its Black Sea "exclusive economic zone".

If this had happened just a few nautical miles to the west, Article 5 of the Nato treaty could have been triggered. The article defines an armed attack on one member of the military alliance as an attack on all.

"Escalation in the Black Sea is steadily increasing," Bulgaria's defence minister later told reporters after speaking to his counterparts in Romania and Turkey. "We see this conflict drawing ever closer to our territorial waters."

"We assume the drones are Russian," he said, as it would have been "illogical" for Ukraine to target its own ships.

Rumen Radev had earlier asked Nato and the EU for technical assistance in investigating the previous attacks that took place on 6 October, indicating it was unclear who was behind them.

Radev came to office during the summer and although he has rejected suggestions that he is "pro-Russian", his government has until now avoided blaming Moscow.

Ukraine has directly accused Russia of staging the latest attacks and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen spoke on Tuesday of the Black Sea becoming "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine. This is unacceptable".

Russia's military has not publicly commented on the issue. It has recently intensified its strikes on vessels in the Black Sea, particularly the western side, as part of its war against Ukraine.

The same day that two ships were targeted off Bulgaria last week, Ukraine hit an oil tanker in the Russian Black Sea port of Sochi.

Moscow says it is targeting ships delivering weapons and dual-use cargo to Ukrainian ports - and cited attacks in the ports of Mykolaiv and Chornomorsk last week, along with one in the Black Sea.

However, Kyiv and its European allies say merchant vessels carrying grain and other civilian cargo are being attacked.

Meeting his security chiefs on Tuesday, Bulgaria's prime minister said: "Another attack on merchant ships in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters is absolutely unacceptable".

While the search continued for the rest of the crew from the HS Dignity, Radev said five crew members on board the Chelsea-3 were being treated for minor injuries. The cargo ship is registered in the southern Ukraine port of Odesa.

Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said "Russia's latest attack on commercial vessels near Bulgaria's territorial waters... once again demonstrates Moscow's deliberate disregard for civilian lives and maritime security in the Black Sea".

"The Black Sea is a lifeline for global food security. Russia is attacking it to weaponise hunger and hold the world hostage. This must be met with strength," he added.

Both Russia and Ukraine are major grain-exporting countries and Turkey has called on both countries to halt attacks in the Black Sea.

Moscow has repeatedly rejected calls by the US and Europe for a naval ceasefire in the Black Sea, blaming Ukraine for attacking Russian merchant ships in the area.

Russian President Vladimir Putin launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, and Moscow currently controls about 20% of Ukrainian territory.

items.title: Amazon ha un milione di robot: il lavoro umano è a rischio?
items.summary: Amazon supera un milione di robot nei magazzini tra intelligenza artificiale, sicurezza e dubbi sul futuro del lavoro.
items.content:
Ormai nei magazzini più tecnologicamente avanzati, i robot rappresentano la normalità. E così, si muovono tra i scaffali, smistano pacchi e preparano spedizioni, con una naturalezza che solo qualche anno fa sembra improbabile. Da un lato questa sembra essere l'evoluzione ideale, ma dall'altro la morte del lavoro umano sembra inesorabilmente avvicinarsi. Questa tecnologia sta raggiungendo un tale livello di raffinatezza, che la rende in grado di coprire sempre più ruoli, ma è tutto oro ciò che luccica?

Tutto ciò ha un risvolto positivo anche sull'uomo, sui rischio di infortuni gravi ad esempio, ma se si arrivasse a un punto in cui fossero le macchine a stabilire il ritmo di lavoro delle persone, per poi successivamente soppiantarle del tutto?

La domanda si fa sempre più attuale, anche in funzione di quanto sta accadendo nei centri logistici di Amazon, che ha ormai superato il milione di robot operativi. Si tratta di una flotta impressionante, che badate bene, è destinata a crescere ulteriormente grazie a nuovi stabilimenti produttivi negli Stati Uniti.

Il top gamma piu completo? Honor Magic 8 Pro, compralo al miglior prezzo da Aliexpress.com a 797 euro.

items.summary: https://www.apple.com/safari/switch/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50072286 Points: 125 # Comments: 193
items.content:
Apple is kicking off a new campaign today to promote Safari’s benefits over Chrome. With a new “Switch to Safari” page on its website and a pair of new YouTube videos, Apple wants everyone to know Safari is “a more powerful and private browser than Chrome.”

On the new website, Apple touts several advantages of Safari over Chrome, including better battery life, stronger privacy protections, and faster performance.

The site also includes a side-by-side Safari vs Chrome comparison chart, alongside details on features including Reader Mode, Notify Me , Profiles, Apple Pay, and more.

Ditching chrome should be first advice for everyone on every platform and yet many places including governments make it their standard then other departments classify it as a high security risk and ban it

In addition to the new “Switch to Safari” website, Apple has also published two YouTube videos showcasing Safari’s Distraction Control and Intelligent Tracking Prevention .

You can check out the new page on Apple’s website and watch the new videos below. This is only the latest example of Apple’s head-to-head promotion of Safari vs Chrome. Earlier this year, the company launched a new “Privacy on iPhone” campaign promoting Safari as the more private alternative to Chrome.

Do you prefer Safari or Chrome on your Mac? Let us know down in the comments.

items.title: Questo è Apple HomeView, il display per la casa con Siri AI. In Europa non arriva
items.summary: Apple ha presentato HomeView, un display da 7 pollici con Siri AI che unisce smart speaker, centro di controllo della casa e terminale FaceTime. Prezzo di 299 dollari, preordini aperti, disponibilità dal 13 novembre. Per ora, però, non verrà venduto nell’Unione Europea. ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Dopo anni di indiscrezioni, Apple ha finalmente ufficializzato HomeView, la versione di HomePod con display. Ricorda molto da vicino l’iMac G4, uno dei prodotti più iconici di Apple, disegnato da Jonathan Ive ed entrato nella collezione permanente del MoMA. Questa volta appeso al braccio in acciaio non c’è un monitor LCD da 15” ma uno schermo Liquid Retina da 7 pollici , sempre collegato a una base con altoparlante a cupola in alluminio.

Trattandosi di un prodotto da esporre in casa, Apple ha preparato quattro versioni (silver, starlight, rose pink e space gray, dotate di cavo coordinato) e ha previsto anche una versione da montare a muro per ingressi e corridoi.

HomeView non arriverà in Europa, almeno non subito . Apple dice chiaramente che “ HomeView non è disponibile per la vendita nell’Unione Europea in quanto Siri AI non è al momento disponibile su iOS nell’UE. Apple sta collaborando attivamente con l’Unione Europea per individuare una soluzione ”.

Lo precisiamo perché, sebbene a oggi iOS e iPadOS debbano sottostare al regolamento europeo per i mercati digitali, il DMA, e proprio su quel regolamento il lancio dell’assistente AI su iPhone e iPad sia stato bloccato, ci sono sistemi operativi Apple come macOS che invece non hanno problemi: Siri AI su Mac in Europa c’è, e gli italiani non hanno potuto provarlo solo perché ancora manca la lingua italiana. Impostando la lingua del Mac in inglese, Siri AI si attiva e funziona regolarmente.

Perché quindi HomeView, che non è né un iPhone né un iPad, non arriva in Europa?

Tutto va ricercato nel modo in cui Apple fa funzionare HomeView, che resta un dispositivo da 299 euro sul quale non girano gli stessi modelli di Apple Intelligence che girano su iPhone e iPad, e che probabilmente non ha nemmeno la RAM e un processore adeguati per farli girare.

Quando Apple dice che, con un iPhone o un iPad compatibili con Apple Intelligence, HomeView può attingere al personal context dell’utente (Calendario, Messaggi, app) e agire tra le app, ci sta dicendo che la vera esperienza agentica la si ottiene solo quando è l’iPhone (o l’iPad) connesso a gestire la parte IA ; senza questi due prodotti si ottiene un’esperienza depotenziata.

L’azienda spiega che chi non ha un dispositivo compatibile ottiene comunque risposte generali, può sostenere conversazioni più naturali e può anche cercare meglio la musica, ma è chiaro che HomeView usa l’iPhone e i dati dell’iPhone per capire chi ha davanti, cosa vuole la persona che ha davanti ed essere più preciso e proattivo.

Ci sono comunque speranze: l’Europa chiede ad Apple di concedere agli assistenti virtuali di terze parti lo stesso accesso ai dati di cui dispone Siri AI, ma Apple vuole poter garantire la privacy e la sicurezza che i clienti si aspettano dai suoi prodotti. L’azienda dice di essersi presentata al tavolo con i commissari europei con un approccio costruttivo e con una serie di proposte che permetterebbero l’interoperabilità con terze parti tutelando privacy e sicurezza (i Trusted Agent, o TOSA), e sembra che Bruxelles condivida questi obiettivi. Portare Siri AI e tutti i suoi prodotti ai clienti europei resta, secondo quanto ci ha detto Apple, una priorità.

Tornando a HomeView, il dispositivo riconosce fino a sei persone dal volto e per ciascuna mostra una Home Screen personale con app e widget, un po’ come fa già Echo Show. Messaggi, FaceTime, Calendario, Reminders e Find My, quindi i dati più sensibili, compaiono solo se l’utente è stato riconosciuto e se il suo iPhone o il suo iPad sono in prossimità del dispositivo e sono stati sbloccati di recente.

Le foto condivise e la musica restano invece accessibili a tutti coloro che hanno accesso fisico al dispositivo.

Dal punto di vista dell’architettura è molto simile al nuovo Apple Watch, con funzioni locali che si appoggiano però all’iPhone, vedi Siri Recap. Anche per HomeView arrivano le Secure Exclaves, spazi di esecuzione isolati che elaborano i dati di fotocamera e microfono separatamente dal resto del sistema.

Non si tratta di elementi separati del chip fisico, come il Secure Enclave che gestisce i dati del FaceID, ma di piccoli sistemi capaci di elaborare dati senza però essere visibili, né al software di HomeView, né alle app, né all’utente, né ad Apple stessa.

Particolarmente curato l’audio: ci sono due driver full-range nel display con Spatial Audio, un woofer down-firing e due radiatori passivi force-cancelling nella base, con audio computazionale che ottimizza volume e bassi in tempo reale. La versione a muro ha due driver e una taratura dedicata che tiene conto della parete posteriore vicina.

Sul fronte delle app, HomeView resta un ecosistema chiuso, almeno per ora. Apple cita Music, Podcasts, News e TV e aggiunge il supporto ad app audio e video di terze parti “compatibili”, senza spiegare quali siano né come gli sviluppatori possano rendere compatibile la propria. Apple non parla di un App Store dedicato né di un SDK, con un approccio che ricorda più una categoria curata da Apple, sul modello di CarPlay, che una piattaforma aperta come tvOS.

Piccola chicca: HomeView rileva anche il suono di allarmi fumo e monossido di carbonio e avvisa su iPhone, iPad o Apple Watch. Precisiamo che il rilevamento riguarda il suono: non è il dispositivo a essere dotato di sensore.

HomeView costa 299 dollari sia nella versione da tavolo sia in quella a muro, dove però servono supporti particolari che costano 59,95 dollari per la versione USB e 79,95 dollari per quella AC. A inizio 2027 arriverà anche quella Power Over Ethernet.

items.title: How to engineer an AI harness for game development
items.summary: Article URL: https://kylekukshtel.com/ai-harness-engineering-game-development-claude-code Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50072120 Points: 92 # Comments: 37
items.content:
I gave a 45 minute presentation entitled “ Your Game Is A Harness” as part of Indie Rodeo in Calgary on 9/12/26. After speaking with a lot of people after my talk, I thought it would be good to more broadly share the ideas I presented there in a form that could be enjoyed by people beyond just those who attended the conference.

Also, because I talk about AI a lot on this blog, people assume I use AI to write. This is not true! Everything below is 100% human authored, with me writing the post with basically only the slides I presented as a reference (this is not a transcription). As much as I enjoy using AI to write code and tools, I get a similar enjoyment out of writing “ the old way”, especially as I have no reason to try and make any part of this process more efficient.

So with that all out of the way, I present to you my first ever blogification of a talk I gave. Enjoy!

[I give a small introduction to myself and my own work, that I’m omitting here, as you’re on my website]

I want to talk about using LLMs in game development. Not one-shot type demos that look cool on Twitter, but like real development. Where you’re working eight hours a day, 5 days a week, etc.

And before I get into it, I think it’s useful to level set about LLMs. Or at least get into some basics so the rest of what I talk about here makes sense. I recognize that for a lot of this people this will be review, so if you just want to get into the dev-loop stuff, scroll down to the next section.

My journey into using LLMs for dev work started with a moodboarding site I made called mood.site . This was pre “ agentic” anything, but I wanted to test and see if ChatGPT at the time could actually code anything. The process was a lot of me just blindly copy/pasting code into ChatGPT’s web interface. The process sucked, but I was surprised at the results. I built the site! It worked! I still needed to verify a fair amount of stuff myself, but it was enough to convert me. If I didn’t have access to an LLM I wouldn’t have been able to make that site happen in near the amount of time it ended up taking me (~2-3 weeks of nights, probably like 20 hours total). I’d probably still be working on building the first version today.

Since then, mood has become something of a testbed for me moving through LLM stuff (and a mildly successful project on its own!), and has inspired me to kick up lots of other projects that use similar stacks. Additionally, LLMs have gotten better, especially with things like Claude Code and later Claude models. From my own experience, I feel like now there is very little, if anything, I think an LLM can’t do when it comes to a web-based stack.

It could be easy to then say LLMs can do everything , as so much of software is web software. But whenever I tried to use an LLM on building a non-web game thing , it was this resounding takeaway:

Any time I tried to use an LLM for a game-y thing, it would fall over. Maybe this is my own bias. I’ve been a game programmer for nearly 15 years, I think I know how things work. I can sniff out “ bad” game code a mile away. But when it comes to Svelte web-apps, I’m decidedly less well versed and am inclined to think that whatever code the LLM produces is “ good”. Maybe it’s actually garbage. But there is reason to believe the Svelte and web-stack stuff is quality, in part due to the fact that there are LOTS of high quality web projects with their source available online. Comparatively for games, I imagine there are orders of magnitude less data to train on.

Not only this, but games have a lot of stuff in them that isn’t code. Games aren’t just about putting static images and text in a layout. There are tons of things in games that aren’t easily representable by code. AND then on top of that there is all the same text layout stuff of web, but only as a subset of the 100 other systems a game needs to handle.

This is part of the reason why a lot of people have been making games in Three.js — they can easily represent assets as plain boxy primitives and skip a lot of the asset generation/conforming work and processing normally required for games. As a result, a lot of that stuff is slop because it lacks any real authorial voice outside of whatever the LLM median is.

A key idea of the one-shot Three.JS workflow (as well as LLMs proficiency at building web apps) is that everything is code. By having stuff as code, it’s very easy for an LLM to be able to reason about it, make changes, etc.

However for traditional games, this is not the case. Or at least the full story. Games obviously have code, but there is a lot of other stuff that is not code. This means that there are key components of games that are effectively opaque to an LLM . If your game then relies on the effective puppeting and transforming of that opaque stuff, then an LLM is going to fall over when trying to work on your game.

I think a lot of the gamedev community maybe gave LLMs a go a bit ago and ran directly into this. The “ LLMs are bad/not useful/etc.” sentiment (massive caveat here, just talking about capability specifically and not potential society-ending implications) came from running headfirst into these limitations.

This is to say that, structurally, LLMs are bad at reading games. At least in their default state.

Any call/prompt to any LLM service breaks down into three basic components. A system prompt, an assistant prompt, and a user prompt:

System prompt: Generic text shared across all users of a service. This usually describes the basics of the LLM itself, with something like “ You are Opus 5, an intelligent Large Language Model created by Anthropic…”. This isn’t to say these aren’t important (they are), but more that they aren’t super-relevant to our use case. You can see some examples of posted (and exfiltrated) system prompts for models here .

Assistant prompt: This is kind of a sidecar prompt section meant to help guide the AI in terms of what it is responding to. You can think of it basically as the model’s basic “ interaction” vector with your prompt, and represents something like the model’s “ response” to the user based on some input. You usually do not have to think about this.

User Prompt : This is really The Thing. Most any input you put into any AI tool goes here. Any submitted chat, code, etc. gets dumped into this section. When people talk about “ context”, they are largely talking about “ how many tokens are stored in the user (and assistant) portion of a prompt”.

It may be easy to think that each chat is a “ fresh” version of the above, but what actually happens is that, as you work with a model in a given session (the bounds of “ session” vary based on what service you are using — this can be a single Claude Code session before closing it, a “ chat” accessible in the side panel of a web hosted model, etc.), every prior message you sent to the model is re-submitted every time you send a message. It’s kind of like playing the old playground game where, on your turn, you have to say everyone else’s thing again before then adding your own thing for the next person to have to add on.

As you do this over and over, you build up the “ context” of the session you’re working in.

This is all well and good, but a key thing to notice here is that you only really are able to address the “ latest” thing in your context (i.e., you submit a new message). Things from previous messages get submitted over and over again to the model. Hence, you want to make sure what’s in your context is “ good”, otherwise you can find yourself in degenerate scenarios where your context becomes polluted due to “ bad” things earlier continually informing new work.

Managing context then is a key thing in working with LLMs, and a new engineering practice called “ context engineering” has emerged in light of these constraints. Context engineering asks “ how can we get the best information into the context, with as little pollution as possible”.

There is a great blog post here on “ ways long contexts fail” that goes a bit more into this, but I’ll highlight the key part here:

Context Engineering itself is a really big topic that is outside the scope of this talk/blog, but we will be using some of the tenets of it here to explore how to help LLMs do a better job working with games.

Said differently, getting LLMs to work well with games is a context problem, not something that is intrinsically linked to how games or LLMs “ are” (or “ aren’t”!).

The complicating factor here though is, games are weird . Or at least: we have no real template to build a game. We have game engines, but there is effectively 0 standardized tooling for anything, in part because every game manifests its own needs differently from one another.

This is acutely unique to games (imo), but it manifests enough in other technological domains that a new concept has emerged in order to get agents to effectively “ work” with whatever your work product is: Harnesses.

The general idea of a Harness is that it’s some set patterns of actions an agent is meant to take in response to some well (or loosely) defined expected input. You’re probably already using a harness like Claude Code, but these can be augmented, extended, distilled, abstracted, etc. to better support the specific work you are trying to do. There’s also been a LOT of action in this space recently, with many harnesses being built for developing all sorts of things:

items.title: Apple rifà casa: lanciati i nuovi accessori per la smart home sviluppati con LG e Schneider Electric
items.summary: Videocamere, campanelli, serrature, termostati e sensori di temperatura. Configurazione con un tap su iPhone, crittografia end-to-end e nessuna app di terze parti. In vendita da dicembre, anche sull'Apple Store italiano ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Le indiscrezioni circolate nei giorni scorsi si sono rivelate sostanzialmente corrette, perché i prodotti presentati da Apple all'evento Welcome Home di oggi corrispondono a quelli mostrati dai leak. La nuova Apple Home Collection comprende videocamere per interni ed esterni, un campanello con videocamera, una serratura e due termostati con i relativi sensori, progettati insieme a LG Electronics e Schneider Electric per dare nuova spinta alla casa smart di Apple.

Ogni dispositivo si configura con un tap su iPhone, come accade con un HomePod, e si controlla dall'app Casa o con Siri. I dati sono protetti da crittografia end-to-end, che stando ad Apple impedisce l'accesso a LG, a Schneider Electric e alla stessa Apple, mentre il supporto a Thread , il protocollo di rete a basso consumo pensato per la domotica, tiene in piedi i collegamenti anche quando cade il Wi-Fi. C’è anche Matter.

Molto semplici i nomi dei dispositivi, come “campanello con videocamera”, “videocamera con faretti”, “videocamera per esterni”, "videocamera per interni”.

Tuttavia, il numero di videocamere coperte dipende dallo spazio acquistato , perché il piano da 50 GB ne supporta una, quello da 200 GB fino a cinque e quello da 2 TB un numero illimitato.

Molto più stretti i limiti dei riassunti dei filmati generati da Apple Intelligence, che secondo la pagina di supporto di Apple coprono una sola videocamera con il piano da 2 TB, che costa 9,99 euro al mese, due con quello da 6 TB a 29,99 euro e cinque con quello da 12 TB a 59,99 euro. Apple precisa comunque che il numero di videocamere supportate potrebbe cambiare nel tempo.

Il campanello affianca a un sensore frontale a 2,5K anche un secondo sensore Full HD rivolto verso il basso per inquadrare i pacchi , mentre la videocamera da interni affida la privacy a un movimento meccanico, perché si solleva per inquadrare la stanza quando l'utente la guarda dall'app Casa e torna a inclinarsi verso il basso, interrompendo il monitoraggio, appena qualcuno del nucleo famigliare rientra in casa.

Per le videocamere non è stato indicato chiaramente un supporto a Matter. Questa categoria, tra l’altro è gestita dal layer solo con la versione 1.5 da novembre dell’anno scorso.

Con la serratura Smart Deadbolt di LG , Apple porta in casa l'Ultra Wideband, la tecnologia radio che misura con precisione la distanza tra i dispositivi usato soprattutto gli AirTag, e che qui sblocca la porta quando ci si avvicina con la chiave di casa su iPhone o Apple Watch ; ci sono anche un tastierino PIN e una chiave di riserva, e il funzionamento in locale, compatibile con Matter e Aliro , non dipende dalla connessione internet.

I termostati di LG e Schneider Electric si regolano invece con la funzione Temperatura adattiva in base alla presenza delle persone in casa, agli orari di riposo e ai periodi di assenza; e per misurare temperatura e umidità in più stanze possono contare su sensori autonomi, venduti sia da LG sia da Schneider Electric , oppure su quelli già integrati in HomePod e HomePod mini. Termostati e sensori sono compatibili con Matter.

L’arrivo dei dispositivi sull'Apple Store online italiano, nell'app Apple Store e nei negozi Apple, è previsto a inizio 2027 . Nell'elenco dei prezzi, però, i singoli prodotti compaiono solo per Stati Uniti, Canada e, nel caso delle videocamere, Regno Unito. Per l'Italia non ci sono ancora listini in euro.

Negli Stati Uniti il campanello costa 249,95 dollari, la videocamera con faretti 399,95, quella per esterni 299,95 e quella per interni 199,95, mentre la serratura parte da 349,95 dollari e i termostati da 199,95.

items.title: Ecco la nuova Apple TV 4K: arrivano Siri AI (ma non nell'UE) e chip A19
items.summary: Tre microfoni far-field per i comandi vocali a mani libere, supporto a quattro HomePod e la nuova Siri, che però in Italia (e in tutta l'UE) non avremo al lancio ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Apple ha svelato la nuova generazione di Apple TV 4K come parte della nuova offerta di dispositivi per la casa connessa. La nuova generazione introduce soprattutto Siri AI, che però non arriverà nell'UE: Apple e la Commissione Europea stanno ancora discutendo su come integrare la nuova versione di Siri. Di base, la questione riguarda iOS e iPadOS, in quanto piattaforma "gatekeeper"; probabilmente, le funzionalità legate a iPhone hanno impattato anche su Apple TV 4K.

I preordini sono già aperti, mentre la disponibilità è prevista dal 13 novembre. In Italia Apple TV 4K sarà proposta a 349 euro .

Gli utenti possono usare Siri AI con la nuova Apple TV 4K per cercare film e serie attraverso domande formulate in linguaggio naturale. Durante la visione, Siri AI può rispondere a domande contestuali come il luogo in cui è stata girata una serie oppure se un determinato contenuto sia adatto a un quindicenne. In questi casi le informazioni vengono mostrate attraverso un riquadro più discreto, senza interrompere completamente ciò che si sta guardando. Con un iPhone compatibile con Apple Intelligence, Siri AI può utilizzare il contesto personale dell’utente. Apple porta come esempio la richiesta "Riproduci la serie consigliata da Alinda", riferendosi alle informazioni disponibili sul dispositivo associato.

Mancando Siri AI in Italia e in tutta l'Unione Europea, che è una delle principali novità di questa generazione, per valutare le novità disponibili bisogna fare dunque riferimento all'hardware.

Per esempio, la nuova Apple TV 4K integra tre microfoni far-field. Questo permette di richiamare Siri con "Hey Siri" oppure semplicemente "Siri" senza utilizzare il telecomando. Un sistema di cancellazione dell’eco cerca di isolare la voce anche mentre il televisore sta riproducendo audio.

Soprattutto, all'interno viene introdotto il chip A19 . Apple dichiara prestazioni CPU fino al 50% superiori rispetto alla generazione precedente e una GPU fino a due volte più veloce. Il miglioramento dovrebbe tradursi soprattutto in navigazione più rapida, animazioni più fluide e prestazioni superiori nei giochi. A19 integra un decoder AV1 dedicato.

È stato aggiornato anche il Siri Remote : il design rimane sostanzialmente invariato, ma arriva il supporto a Dov’è con Precision Finding e la possibilità di far emettere un suono al telecomando quando non si riesce a trovarlo. È compatibile anche con Apple TV HD.

La Apple TV 4K di quarta generazione può essere abbinata a quattro HomePod mini 2 per creare un sistema surround. I diffusori lavorano insieme alla Apple TV per determinare automaticamente la propria posizione nella stanza e calibrare tempi e livelli dell’audio.

La stessa configurazione può essere realizzata anche utilizzando quattro HomePod di seconda generazione, a condizione che la coppia anteriore e quella posteriore utilizzino diffusori dello stesso modello.

La nuova Apple TV 4K continua a funzionare come hub per Apple Home, ma Apple Intelligence aggiunge alcune nuove funzioni. Con videocamere compatibili, il sistema può generare descrizioni dell’attività rilevata e riepiloghi delle notifiche. In presenza di un campanello smart, per esempio, sul televisore può comparire l’immagine della persona alla porta e l’utente può parlarle oppure controllare altri dispositivi della casa, come una serratura compatibile.

Il dispositivo integra Wi-Fi e Thread e supporta automazioni, modalità ospite e l’elaborazione locale di HomeKit Secure Video.

Per la privacy, Apple TV 4K e il chip A19 utilizzano le cosiddette Secure Exclaves, ambienti isolati nei quali vengono elaborati i dati provenienti dai microfoni. Secondo Apple, le informazioni elaborate in queste aree non sono accessibili a tvOS, alle app, all’utente o alla stessa società. Le richieste Siri possono essere elaborate direttamente sul dispositivo oppure attraverso Private Cloud Compute. In quest’ultimo caso Apple afferma che i dati non vengono conservati né resi accessibili alla società.

items.title: Ex-president named leader of new DR Congo rebel coalition
items.summary: Joseph Kabila had previously denied having links to the M23 rebels, which control much of eastern DR Congo.
items.content:
Former Congolese President Joseph Kabila has been named the leader of a new rebel coalition seeking to oust the government.

The Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN) said it aimed to coordinate "resistance forces" to end "tyranny" in Democratic Republic of Congo and would pursue the goal "by all means, including force".

Its unveiling on Monday is the clearest indication so far of Kabila's direct involvement in an armed movement a year after he was sentenced to death in absentia for treason. He had previously denied having links to the M23 rebel group.

Claude Ibalanky, the coalition's adviser, announced the group's leadership at a press conference at Kabila's residence in Goma, the largest city in eastern DR Congo, which has been under the control of the M23 since last year.

Video released by the group showed Kabila signing documents at the group's declaration along with other leaders.

M23 leader Sultani Makenga will serve as one of Kabila's four deputies in the new movement. The other three also come from the AFC-M23 alliance which last year seized much of mineral-rich eastern DR Congo.

The announcement of the new group comes days after Kabila delivered an address in which he said he would set out how Congolese people should act to "rescue" their country.

On Friday, Kabila accused President Félix Tshisekedi's government of disregarding proposals he had put forward last year, including some aimed at ending the conflict in eastern DR Congo.

Kabila also accused the government of undermining constitutional rule, mismanaging the economy and failing to improve security. He further alleged arbitrary arrests of political opponents and military officers.

Kabila, 55, ruled DR Congo from 2001 until January 2019, when Tshisekedi took office following a disputed election.

The two were once political allies, forming an informal power-sharing arrangement after the transfer of power. They later fell out and Kabila went into self-imposed exile in 2023 before returning to Goma last year.

The former president had remained largely out of public view for several years but has become increasingly critical of his successor's administration.

The formation of the new coalition comes at an uncertain time in a country that has been wracked by violence for decades.

More than 100 militia groups are active in eastern DR Congo amid ethnic tensions and fighting for political power and control of lucrative natural resources.

The UN and Western governments accuse Rwanda of backing the M23 and controlling the rebels.

Rwanda denies supporting the M23 despite overwhelming evidence, and says its military presence in eastern DR Congo is a defensive measure against threats posed by Congolese armed groups.

Tshisekedi's second term ends in 2028 but in May he said that elections, which are due then, may not be held because of the conflict.

He also hinted that he may seek re-election for a third term "if the people want".

The parliament has since passed a bill that could pave the way for a referendum that could remove the constitution's two-term limit.

Last month, authorities clashed with protesters holding demonstrations in the capital against the proposed changes.

Richard Moncrieff, who monitors Africa's Great Lakes region for the International Crisis Group (ICG) says the new coalition is aimed at trying to enlarge the rebellion.

He argues that through his "higher profile", Kabila hopes to get support from people dissatisfied with Tshisekedi "beyond the very narrow political base that the M23 enjoys".

The analyst says this appears to be Kabila's objective, to draw more senior Congolese army officers to his side and "lessen the reliance of the M23 on its Rwandan backers".

Kabila came to power after the assassination of his father Laurent Kabila, who headed a national rebellion in the 1990s, backed by Rwanda. His forces marched across the country, starting in the east, before taking over in the capital Kinshasa, some 1,500km (1,000 miles) away.

Moncrieff says Kabila is drawing on that past to proclaim the illegitimacy of Tshisekedi's government.

He however says it won't be easy to seize power like his father, partly because the US has imposed sanctions on Kabila, which he says presumes American support for DR Congo's government.

In May the US imposed sweeping sanctions on Kabila, accusing him of backing the M23, providing financial support, encouraging defections from the Congolese army. Kabila said the measures were unjustified and politically motivated.

The US said they were part of a wider effort to support last year's peace deal between DR Congo and Rwanda that it brokered.

The latest events show peace negotiations are "going nowhere and attempting to gain control on the ground is the priority for all parties," the ICG analyst says.
